parsed_response.reasoning: The diff confirms the mechanism: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now loops over every destination in destinationCalendar and calls createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId), which passes credential.id to calendar.createEvent. However, only GoogleCalendarService actually consumes credentialId to select the right calendar (calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)). BaseCalendarService, LarkCalendarService, and Office365CalendarService were changed only to destructure destinationCalendar[0] (e.g. `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and the filter `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`), ignoring the per-credential parameter. So on collective bookings each host's credential is still aimed at the first host's externalId — for CalDAV, the calendar filter can match nothing in that credential's calendar list, silently skipping the event; for Lark/O365 the request targets host 1's calendar with host 2's credential. This is a real correctness defect introduced/exposed by this diff.

judged_text: Calendar services that did not gain the credentialId parameter (BaseCalendarService, LarkCalendarService, Office365CalendarService) still resolve the target calendar from destinationCalendar[0] on every per-credential createEvent call, so for collective bookings host 2+'s credentials are aimed at host 1's calendar externalId. For CalDAV/Lark/O365 collective bookings the second and later hosts' events are silently skipped (the BaseCalendarService filter matches nothing in their own calendar list) or fail against another host's calendar id, so only the first host's calendar materializes the event — the exact multi-host case this PR set out to fix.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and updates the `Calendar` interface to `createEvent(event, credentialId)` (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts) and `CalendarManager.createEvent` now calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. However, multiple calendar services shown in the diff still (a) do not accept/use `credentialId` and (b) derive the target calendar solely from `destinationCalendar[0]`: BaseCalendarService filters calendars using `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then matches only that externalId; LarkCalendarService and Office365CalendarService similarly take `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]` and use its `externalId`. Meanwhile, EventManager now can create events per-destination (looping `event.destinationCalendar` and selecting credentials per destination), but it passes the same `event` object (containing all destinations) into each per-credential create, so non-Google services will still always target the first destination externalId. This makes collective/multi-host bookings likely to either write all events into host1’s calendar or skip/fail for later hosts when the first externalId isn’t present for their credential (exactly as described for BaseCalendarService’s filter).
